steps.title: Recognizing trust marks
steps.body: Trustworthy Dutch web shops often show a Thuiswinkel Waarborg logo at the bottom of the website. Click it: it should link to a real, valid registration.

steps.title: Don't know the shop yet?
steps.body: Ordering from a shop you don't know yet? Search the name together with the word 'reviews' or 'scam' to see what others write about it.

steps.title: Checking contact details
steps.body: A trustworthy web shop always has a findable address, phone number, and company registration number on the website (often at the bottom, under 'Contact' or 'About us'). Missing entirely? Be careful.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Browse a web shop below and look for its contact details and trust mark.

steps.title: Adding something to your cart
steps.body: Click 'Add to cart' or 'Order' on a product. Then go to your cart (often an icon top right) to review and complete your order.

steps.title: Paying safely with iDEAL
steps.body: iDEAL is the most widely used, safe payment method in the Netherlands: you pay directly through your own banking app, without entering your card details anywhere else.

steps.title: Keeping the confirmation email
steps.body: After ordering you'll receive a confirmation email with your order number. Keep it — you'll need it if something goes wrong or if you want to return something.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Add a product to your cart on a web shop of your choice, without completing the order.

steps.title: Track & trace
steps.body: The confirmation email often includes a track & trace link. Click it to see where your parcel is and when it will be delivered.

steps.title: Your right to change your mind
steps.body: When shopping online in the Netherlands, you usually have 14 days to return something, no reason needed — even if there's nothing wrong with the product.

steps.title: Returning something
steps.body:
1. Go to 'My orders' on the website
  2. Choose the order and click 'Return'
  3. Follow the instructions for the return label
  4. Drop off the parcel at the indicated point (often a parcel point or delivery service)

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Look up a web shop's return policy: how many days do they allow?

steps.title: Recognizing fake reviews
steps.body: Are all the reviews very short, overly positive, and posted around the same date? That can point to fake reviews. Also read the critical reviews — they often give a more honest picture.

steps.title: Too good to be true
steps.body: A new TV for next to nothing? Be suspicious of prices far lower than at well-known stores. Compare the price with at least two other shops.

steps.title: Only safe payment methods
steps.body: Is advance payment only accepted via bank transfer, with no iDEAL or credit card option? That's a major warning sign — with a scam, you usually can't get that money back.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Look at the reviews of a product you're interested in, and check whether they seem honest and varied.
